picked.t: [베트남 주간 이슈] SK 원유 터지고 UOB VN성장률 9.2% 상향…베트남, 모빌리티·디지털 타고 거침없는 질주
picked.body: 싱가포르 UOB가 베트남의 올해 경제성장률 전망치를 9.2%로 대폭 끌어올렸다. 빈패스트가 25개월 연속 시장 1위를 지키며 북미·아시아 모빌리티 영토를 넓히는 가운데, SK어스온은 베트남 광구에서 첫 원유를 뿜어내며 6,000만 배럴 자원 확보의 물꼬를 텄다.  하지만 베트남은 빠른 성장 만큼 명암도 짙어지고 있다. 1㎡당 5,000만 원에 달하는 초호화 아파트 열풍으로 주거 빈부격차가 극에 달하고, 건기철 하노이의 대기오염은 세계 상위권을 기록하며 성장통을 드러냈다.  베트남 주간 경제·산업 동향 포인트 3가지 빈패스트 및 전기차·이륜차 중심의 모빌리티 영토 확장 빈패스트가 25개월 연속 시장 1위를 기록한 데 이어 미국 전기버스 플랫폼 출시 및 필리핀 신형 SUV 예약 개시, 자회사 GSM의 북미 진출 등 글로벌 공략에 속도를 내고 있다. 국내외 완성차 수요가 급증하는 가운데 내연기관 규제와 친환경 전환 기조가 뚜렷해지고 있다. 디지털 인프라 연동 의무화 및 IT·에너지 분야 한·베 협력 심화 정부가 연내 증권·이커머스·SNS 등 12개 분야의 VNeID 연동을 의무화하며 디지털 통제를 강화하는 한편, SK어스온의 국내 광구 첫 원유 생산, 롯데이노베이트의 데이터센터 협력 등 다방면의 공급망·인프라 연계가 강화되고 있다. 부동산 양극화 심화 및 환경·대기질 악화 우려 하노이 아파트 분양 시장의 흡수율이 저조한 반면 초고가 아파트 열풍이 불며 양극화가 심화되고 있고, 하노이의 대기오염이 세계 상위권에 오르며 건기철 환경 이슈가 주요 현안으로 부각됐다. ■ 정치·정책 '디지털 신원 연동 및 생활 규제 강화' 베트남 정부는 증권, 이커머스, SNS 등 12개 주요 분야에 대해 연내 VNeID(국가 디지털 신원) 연동을 의무화하여 온라인 투명성과 보안을 강화한다. 담배위해예방통제법에 따라 술집과 노래방 등 실내 흡연을 전면 금지하는 방안이 추진된다. ■ 매크로 '신차·이륜차 호조 및 경제 성장 상향' 9월 신차 판매량이 전월 대비 38% 급증하는 등 자동차 수요가 강세를 보이며 연간 50만 대 육박 및 사상 최고치 경신 기대감이 커지고 있다. 오토바이 및 전기이륜차 시장이 동반 성장하며 9월 기준 이륜차 총 누적 대수가 300만 대를 돌파했고 휴대폰 수출도 전년 동기 대비 20% 증가했다. ■ 산업·경제 'UOB 성장률 상향 및 숙련 인력난' 싱가포르 UOB는 베트남의 올해 경제성장률 전망치를 기존 8.5%에서 9.2%로 대폭 상향 조정했다. 반면 기업 10곳 중 5곳이 숙련 인력 채용의 어려움을 호소하고 있어 인적 자원 미스매치가 과제로 지적됐다. ■ 기업 '빈패스트 글로벌 확장 및 글로벌 IT 행보' 빈패스트는 9월 2만 3000여 대를 판매해 25개월 연속 시장 1위를 지켰으며, 미국 전기버스 플랫폼 출시 및 필리핀 SUV 예약 개시 등 해외 진출을 본격화했다. 마이크로소프트는 베트남 R&D 인력을 대거 감축했으나 장기적 투자는 지속하겠다는 입장을 밝혔다. ■ 금융·부동산 '암호화폐 급성장과 초고가 아파트 열풍' 베트남 암호화폐 시장 규모가 연간 1,220억 달러로 동남아 2위를 기록한 반면, 하노이 아파트 분양 시장은 3분기 흡수율이 31%에 그치는 등 엇갈린 양상을 보였다. 1㎡당 5,000만 원에 달하는 초호화 아파트와 브랜드레지던스(1만 6,000여 세대, 세계 3위) 열풍이 불며 주거 빈부격차가 심화되고 있다. ■ 하노이·호치민시 '보행교 완공 및 대기오염 문제' 호치민시는 21일 사이공강 양안을 연결하는 보행교 완공 했으며, 하노이는 건기철 진입과 함께 세계 3위의 불명예스러운 대기오염 수치를 기록하며 대책 마련이 시급해졌다. ■ 인프라 '까마우공항 재개장 및 롱탄신공항 점검' 폐쇄 1년여 만에 개보수를 마친 최남단 까마우공항이 다음 달 재개장하며, 12월 개항을 앞둔 롱탄신공항은 항행장비 비행검사 등 주요 시스템 점검에 돌입했다. ■ 사회 '세계 최고 쌀 선정 및 관광 비자 완화' 베트남 쌀 품종 ST25가 '2026년 세계 최고의 쌀' 2위에 선정되었고, 러시아와 중국(냐짱 방문 단체관광객) 대상 무비자 및 비자 면제 조치가 확대되었다. ■ 한-베 이슈 'SK 원유 생산 및 다방면 경제·문화 교류' SK어스온이 베트남 광구에서 첫 원유 생산을 개시하며 6,000만 배럴 자원 확보의 발판을 마련했고, 롯데이노베이트의 데이터센터 사업 확대 및 현대엔지니어링·SK이노베이션의 기후·생태계 복원 사업이 마무리되었다. 하노이 '한국 미식주간' 개최와 봉화군의 이용상 왕자 정착 800주년 기념행사 등 양국 간 문화·인적 교류도 깊어지고 있다.

picked.t: EU provides $11.2M to extend Hanoi metro line
picked.body: The proposed 11-km section is planned to run entirely underground, in conjunction with transit-oriented development (TOD). The Hanoi People’s Committee, in coordination with the French government, the French Development Agency (AFD), the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the European Investment Bank (EIB), held a commemorative plaque unveiling ceremony for Line 3 at Cau Giay Station (S8) on the Nhon–Hanoi Station line on Oct. 19. The event recognized the results of cooperation between Hanoi, the French government and international financial institutions in developing public transport infrastructure, while opening up prospects for further expansion of the capital's urban railway network. According to information released by the partners at the event, the EU has entrusted AFD with managing a 10-million-euro grant to support preparations for extending Metro Line 3 from Hanoi Station to Hoang Mai. The Hanoi People's Committee signed the support program in 2024, and the Hanoi Metropolitan Railway Management Board (MRB), a public agency under the Hanoi People's Committee responsible for planning, managing, and executing the capital's urban railway network, is implementing it, with preparatory activities expected to be completed by the end of 2027. The extension is planned to be approximately 11 km long and run entirely underground in the southern part of the capital. The grant will fund a feasibility study, transit-oriented development planning along the route, research into traffic organization and multimodal connectivity solutions, and efforts to strengthen project implementation capacity. Integrating urban railway development with TOD planning is expected to help reorganize urban space, improve access to public transport and enhance the efficiency of transport infrastructure. It will also provide a basis for studying connections between residential areas, economic centers and service hubs and high-capacity public transport networks. According to the funding partners, investment for construction of the extension is expected to be explored through the Team Europe cooperation mechanism, with the participation of Germany’s KfW Development Bank and cooperation with ADB. The EUR€10 million grant is specifically intended for research and project preparation, not for the total construction cost of the extension. Construction will depend on the study findings, approval procedures and capital mobilization plans in accordance with regulations. At the event, Hanoi People’s Committee Vice Chairman Truong Viet Dung stressed that the metro line is significant beyond its role as a transport project. Each new metro line not only provides a safe and convenient means of travel but also helps ease congestion, reduce environmental pollution, reorganize urban space and connect development centers. The city expressed its appreciation for support from the French Government and international financial institutions, particularly the EU’s 10-million-euro grant through AFD for studying the extension from Hanoi railway station to Hoang Mai. France's Minister Delegate for Francophonie Éléonore Caroit described Metro Line 3 as tangible evidence of the results of cooperation under the Vietnam–France Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. She also highlighted prospects for further cooperation between France, the EU and Vietnam in public transport development, including preparations to extend Metro Line 3 to Hoang Mai. Victoire Vandeville, AFD’s Regional Director for Southeast Asia, said the millions of passenger journeys recorded during the line’s first year of operation demonstrated the effectiveness of cooperation among the partners. AFD reaffirmed its readiness to continue supporting Hanoi in studying and preparing the Metro Line 3 extension with EU assistance. Scott Roberts, ADB Country Director for Vietnam, emphasized that urban railways do more than meet travel needs. They also connect people with employment, education and development opportunities. ADB pledged to continue working with Hanoi and its partners to develop an integrated and accessible urban transport network that meets the capital’s development needs. Metro Line 3 is 12.5 km long and has 12 stations, including eight elevated and four underground stations. The elevated section from Nhon to Cau Giay began commercial operations in August 2024, providing an additional high-capacity public transport option in western Hanoi. According to data from Hanoi Metro included in a statement by the international partners, the elevated section carried approximately 6.4 million passenger journeys in its first year of operation, with an on-time performance rate of 99%. Beyond its transport benefits, international partners have also highlighted the project’s contribution to reducing greenhouse gas emissions. picked.t: 호치민시 ‘사이공강 보행교’ 내년 뗏(설)연휴 개통…21일 주교량 연결
picked.body: 베트남 호치민시에 들어설 사이공강 보행교 조감도. (조감도=초다이-타카시니와아키텍트 및 초타디키소지반베트남 컨소시엄) 베트남 호치민시의 사이공강을 가로질러 도심과 투티엠(Thu Thiem)신도시를 연결하는 보행교가 이르면 내년 뗏(Tet 설) 연휴 개통될 것으로 전해졌다. 보행교의 핵심 구조물인 주교량은 지난 19일 박당부두(Bach Dang Wharf) 인근 공사 현장에 도착해 설치 작업을 앞두고 있다. 사이공강 보행교 건설사업의 후원사인 누티푸드(Nutifood)는 “21일 상판 연결 작업이 진행될 것”이라고 지난 19일 밝혔다. 누티푸드에 따르면, 사이공강 보행교의 현재 공정률은 90%에 도달한 상태로, 주교량 연결 작업이 끝나면, 시공사는 난간과 조명, 에스컬레이터·엘리베이터 설치 등 남은 작업을 마무리할 계획이다. 예상 개통 시점은 내년 뗏 연휴 중이다. 지난해 3월 착공된 사이공강 보행교는 사이공강을 가로질러 호치민시 옛 1군과 투티엠신도시를 잇는 길이 720m, 너비 6~11m, 경간 187m의 교량으로, 1조 동(약 3,850만 달러)에 달하는 사업비는 영유아식품기업 누티푸드가 후원했다 현지에서는 니파야자(Nipa palm)의 잎을 닮은 사이공강 보행교의 모양이 독특해 완공시 호치민시의 새로운 랜드마크가 될 것으로 기대를 모으고 있다. 니파야자는 꽃대가 돋아나는 모습이 죽순과 닮았다 하여 한국에서는 해죽순으로 불리기도 한다. 보행교는 탁 트인 전망으로 설계됐으며, 자전거도로와 장애인을 위한 도로를 갖췄다. 또한 긴급 상황에 대응할 수 있도록 구급차가 통행할 수 있는 도로도 갖춰진다. 사이공강 보행교를 사이공강을 가로질러 건설되는 최초의 보행자 전용 다리로, 개통 시 도심과 투티엠신도시를 잇는 새로운 경로와 함께 지역민과 관광객을 위한 강변문화공간이 보다 확대될 것으로 기대를 모은다.

picked.t: Managers bear the burden of fixing employees' AI-generated errors
picked.body: Over a year ago, the 40-year-old woman’s company sacked half its employees after integrating artificial intelligence into its operations. The team shrank but the workload remained very high, and so the employees resorted to use of AI. AI-generated stuff often looks good on the surface but carries huge risks. In late 2025, an employee used AI to write an advertisement, and ended up conflating technical specifications of two different car models. The error forced the company to pay compensation to the client and lose 30% of the contract value. After this, Dung banned her staff from using AI at work, but the resultant slow progress forced her to lift the ban in just a week. Now, to ensure quality, she spends an extra five to 10 minutes on each report, verifying every point and cross-checking data. In the past, she used to get only 10 of them in a day, and had plenty of time left to meet clients. Now, she has to go through 40 daily, which needs hours and hours and forces her to take work home every night. "The company cut labor costs thanks to AI, but I’m the one picking up the extra load," she says. This phenomenon of managers cleaning up after their staff is also occurring at Minh Tu’s import-export company in Hai Phong City. Since adopting AI, the company no longer needs to hire translators, and the time required to generate market research reports has dropped from months to a few days. But there are issues. Tu once had to translate a partner's 10-page document herself since the summary an employee had generated using Gemini omitted core details and made up parameters. On another occasion, an employee submitted a market research report containing fabricated figures generated by ChatGPT simply because it "sounded coherent." Instead of focusing on strategic planning, Tu now has to read original foreign-language documents, cross-checking every figure and citation. "The verification step seems insignificant, but takes up a massive amount of time," she says. Dung and Tu’s stories reflect a growing phenomenon known as "workslop", referring to AI-generated products that look polished but lack substance or contain false information. The term gained attention following a survey of over 1,000 U.S. workers published in Harvard Business Review in late 2025. The report revealed that 40% of employees had received "AI slop" within the past month, mostly from colleagues (40%), subordinates (18%), and even superiors (16%). Dealing with this low-quality content took up 15% of their working time, causing 42% of workers to lose trust in their colleagues and 53% to feel frustrated. In Vietnam, data published at the Vietnam AI Productivity Activation event in HCMC on Sept. 23 showed that workers using AI save about 11 to 13 hours per week, but spend an additional 6.4 hours preparing data, editing, and verifying results. In some cases, this creates a "productivity paradox," where the time spent supervising and correcting AI is greater than the time saved by using it. This added workload is often referred to as "AI babysitting", a state where humans must continuously guide, supervise, and correct AI outputs. Notably, a survey by Glean’s Work AI Institute in collaboration with top U.S. universities such as Emory, Stanford, UC Berkeley, and UCL found that 69% of employees admitted to submitting AI-generated work without reviewing or checking it first. Pham Lam Tung, managing director of an AI training center, says many companies have paid a heavy price because their employees let AI do the whole work. At a bank in HCMC, he witnessed a branch director having to redo a financial report after discovering a subordinate fed a blurry scan into AI, causing it to misread the data and make up figures to fill in the blanks. In Hanoi, another bank’s PR team printed large-scale posters of an AI-generated image. It was only after the posters were put up that they noticed the figure in the image had misaligned eyes. "It’s not just employee—many bosses also misuse AI," Tung says. "A startup founder in the northern Bac Ninh Province regularly shared ideas with ChatGPT and received glowing praise. As a result, he shifted strategies every week, forcing his team to constantly revise plans." According to Tung, "AI slop" stems from two causes: employees’ lack of AI-prompting skills while using free versions with limited features or do only the bare minimum due to laziness or burnout. Hong Anh, 28, an advertiser in Hanoi, is part of the second group. Her workload, which doubled after a round of layoffs in 2025, forces her to generate scripts with AI in order to hit her KPI targets. "Between getting fined for missing deadlines and submitting a smooth-sounding draft, hoping the boss won't pay too much attention, I choose to do the latter," she admits. This approach incurs hidden costs: Companies spend resources fixing errors and face legal risks and data leaks; while managers lose trust and employees gradually lose their critical thinking skills. picked.t: Vietnam well positioned to attract higher-value investment: Citi executive
picked.body: Ernesto Torres Cantú oversees Citi's businesses outside North America, giving him a broad perspective on global trade, investment and financial markets. In October, he attended the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund Annual Meetings in Thailand before visiting Vietnam. In this interview, he discusses Vietnam's position in shifting global supply chains, opportunities to attract higher-value investment, the overseas expansion of Vietnamese companies and AI's impact on banking. How is Vietnam positioned amid changes in global trade and supply chains? Global trade is not declining; trade and production are shifting geographically. Businesses are looking beyond costs and prioritizing resilience, speed and flexibility. The Covid-19 pandemic, geopolitical tensions and supply chain disruptions have accelerated efforts to diversify production locations, suppliers and markets. Vietnam is well positioned to benefit. It sits at the heart of Asia's manufacturing ecosystem, has access to global markets through an extensive network of trade agreements and has a domestic market of more than 100 million people. The country also benefits from its strategic location, economic management, ambitious reforms, fiscal discipline and sustained growth. A young, increasingly skilled workforce and rising education levels further strengthen its appeal to investors. Vietnam has established a strong manufacturing base. The next step is to move up the value chain through advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, technology and innovation, while strengthening domestic industries and supply chains. This aligns with the government's goals of improving productivity, accelerating digital transformation and attracting higher-value investment. Citi can help connect Vietnam with the capital, expertise and international markets needed to support these priorities. Vietnam attracted US$50.4 billion in registered foreign direct investment in the first nine months of 2026, up 76% year on year. What is driving this momentum, and how can the country turn it into sustainable growth? The figures reflect strong confidence in Vietnam, but investment volume is only part of the story. The more important question is how investment contributes to productivity, innovation and long-term development. The next wave of foreign investment could extend beyond traditional export manufacturing into advanced electronics, semiconductors, digital infrastructure, data centers, renewable energy, logistics, healthcare and consumer industries. Vietnam's reclassification to secondary emerging-market status should also help deepen its capital markets and broaden access to international investment. Cost competitiveness has been important, but it will not be enough to attract the next generation of investment. Investors will increasingly look for reliable energy supplies, modern infrastructure, skilled workers, predictable regulations and strong domestic suppliers. Vietnam has demonstrated its ability to attract international capital at scale. The opportunity now is to direct more investment into sectors that will shape its next stage of development, particularly advanced manufacturing, semiconductors, digital infrastructure, the energy transition and innovation. During my visit, I met Deputy Prime Minister Nguyen Van Thang, State Bank of Vietnam Deputy Governor Nguyen Ngoc Canh and Deputy Minister of Finance Tran Quoc Phuong. We discussed how Citi could connect public-sector development priorities with international investment through our global network. We also offer expertise in debt strategy, capital markets, investor engagement, hedging and project financing to help governments and institutions mobilize development funding while managing financial risks. Vietnamese companies are increasingly expanding overseas. What will it take for more of them to become successful regional and global players? As Vietnam's economy develops, more local companies are likely to become regional and global leaders. Success requires more than entering new markets: companies must coordinate capital, operations and risk management across countries. Citi works with leading Vietnamese businesses on the financial and operational complexities of cross-border growth. For example, we supported Viettel's expansion in Peru through a $200 million financing facility with a six-year tenor. The financing helped Viettel Peru invest in infrastructure, pursue its long-term objectives and strengthen its position in the market.
